title: End-to-end component and edge coverage matrix

snapshot.scope_note: The matrix describes the main-branch architecture at base_commit. PRs #39–#43 are merged and their implementation is included in this snapshot; their URLs remain as historical evidence.

exhaustive_means: Every known cross-component request, persistence, event-delivery, analytics, and observability boundary is represented by an edge.
Operations sharing the same component pair are grouped only when they have the same contract and failure semantics; materially different operations have separate edges.
Flows are ordered paths through edge IDs, including asynchronous and recovery paths.
A telemetry backend edge is not considered covered unless its producer-to-Collector edge is also represented.

A flow's edge_path is an ordered set of participating interaction boundaries, not necessarily a strict graph walk: synchronous responses return to the caller implicitly, and observability fan-out creates parallel branches.

evidence_semantics.automated_evidence: A test file or function exists. Presence is not a claim that the suite was executed during this matrix update.
evidence_semantics.live_reported_pass: A local runtime validation was reported as passing by the user in the project conversation; the linked PR remains open unless explicitly stated otherwise.
evidence_semantics.reproducible_script: A reproducible script exists; no successful execution is inferred from its presence.
evidence_semantics.documented_only: The behavior is described in repository documentation but no edge-specific automated or live evidence was found.
evidence_semantics.gap: No adequate edge-specific evidence was found for the stated contract.

coverage_levels.covered: The defined contract has relevant automated evidence and sufficient reported live evidence for the stated scope.
coverage_levels.partial: Some contract dimensions are tested, but one or more important operations, runtime boundaries, failure cases, or deployments remain unverified.
coverage_levels.gap: A meaningful contract or failure boundary has no adequate edge-specific verification.
coverage_levels.not_applicable: No test is expected for this edge in the current architecture.

important_caveats: Main currently contains the Gateway implementation from PR #38. PRs #39-#43 are open and unmerged in this snapshot.
A mocked HTTPX transport, ASGI test client, repository integration test, and live Compose test prove different things. They are not interchangeable evidence.
Gateway ingress rejection happens before Order API execution. It does not prove the behavior of an Order Saga after a downstream Inventory failure.
The payment adapter is an internal component of Order API, not a separate deployed service.
The Event Collector is the analytical business-event sink. Loki is the diagnostic-log sink. They are not interchangeable.
Prometheus scrapes the Collector's Prometheus exporter; the Collector does not push metrics into Prometheus.
No CI result is inferred from local test evidence or from the existence of a workflow.

validation_policy: Never mark an edge covered solely because its source/destination appears in a successful happy-path flow.
For HTTP edges, separately record success, domain rejection, dependency 5xx, timeout/connection failure, context propagation and response-loss retry where the operation is idempotent.
For persistence edges, separately record transaction rollback, restart/recovery, concurrency and idempotency.
For async delivery edges, separately record retry, duplicate delivery, acknowledgement loss, lease expiry, quarantine and terminal blocking.
For telemetry edges, prove data is queryable at the destination; exporter configuration alone is not sufficient.
For each live experiment, record exact command, Compose project/stack identity, correlation/request IDs, observed status, durable side effects and restoration steps.
